clue.text: A candidate who fails to keep it is unlikely to get it

definitions.text: A candidate who fails to keep it is unlikely to get it

parts.words: A candidate who fails to keep it is unlikely to get it
parts.note: the first 'it' is a scheduled interview, the second the job itself: a no-show forfeits the post

explanation.surface: A warning to job-seekers that missing the meeting costs them the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word serves twice: an arranged meeting the candidate must keep, and the job the candidate hopes to be given.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a fixed meeting time and a job or post given to someone, and the clue plays on both.

clue.text: One may find their pulses worth taking

definitions.text: One may find their pulses worth taking

parts.words: One may find their pulses worth taking
parts.note: pulses are peas and beans, which grow in shells a cook picks; the surface suggests a doctor taking a pulse

explanation.surface: Sounds like a nurse deciding whose heartbeat is worth checking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulses' looks medical but means edible seeds like peas and lentils, carried in shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas and beans, the legumes called pulses, grow inside seed cases that are gathered when ripe.

clue.text: Single in Lyon, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the word Lyon has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lonely person living unhappily alone in the French city of Lyon.
explanation.definitionFit: Single and sole are synonyms: one alone, with no other.

clue.text: First part of new rise just coming into effect

indicators.note: First part of picks out the opening letter of the word new

parts.note: a rise or climb is an ascent

explanation.surface: A report on a price or pay rise that is only just starting to take effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emerging, only beginning to exist or work, is described by this word.

clue.text: Like those blessed with a worldly inheritance

definitions.text: Like those blessed with a worldly inheritance

parts.words: Like those blessed with a worldly inheritance
parts.note: in the Sermon on the Mount the humble are blessed, for they shall inherit the earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worldly inheritance' is the earth itself, promised in the Beatitudes to the gentle and humble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes promise the earth to the humble and gentle, so the adjective describes those heirs.

clue.text: Every throw-in counts in this game

definitions.text: Every throw-in counts in this game

parts.words: Every throw-in counts in this game
parts.note: throw-in read as a ball thrown in through the hoop, which scores a goal in this team sport

explanation.walkthrough: A throw-in in football merely restarts play; here it means a ball thrown into the hoop's mesh, which is how goals are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game, popular in British schools, where goals are scored only by throwing the ball through a high hoop.

clue.text: Grub to provide food and support

parts.note: to cater is to provide food
a pillar is a support

explanation.surface: Grub, food in slang, seems tied to catering and supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like slang for food, which the surface supports, but it is the insect larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva, and a butterfly's larva is this creature.

clue.text: Others will get lecture supporting Charles II's return

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: the rest are the others
an oration is a formal speech or lecture

explanation.surface: Historians and lecturers discussing the return of the monarchy under Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: The return of the monarchy in 1660, when Charles II took the English throne, is known by this name.

clue.text: Sports spectators that could be barred

definitions.meaning: the attendance or crowd at a match is called the ...
an entrance barrier with bars, or one that could be bolted shut

explanation.surface: Unruly fans who might be banned from the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The number attending a match is its gate; a gate is also a hinged barrier that may be barred.

clue.text: Young people rambling see Scotland

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Teenagers on a walking holiday in the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are young people between childhood and adulthood, called by this name.

clue.text: Achievement one's supporters broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so a word is given by its sound

parts.note: the feet support a person's body

explanation.surface: A sports achievement trumpeted by a team's fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' suggests fans but means the parts that hold you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable accomplishment or exploit, often of skill or daring, is a synonym for achievement.

clue.text: Pupil's joint academic achievement

parts.note: a pupil is a scholar, with the possessive s
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A student's prize won jointly with others.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning, or an award earned for academic merit, is called by this name.

clue.text: A Cornishman making untimely error

indicators.note: making signals that the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: A man from Cornwall committing a blunder of timing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in the wrong period, an error of chronology, is what the word means.

clue.text: Volume that affords satisfaction

definitions.meaning: the amount held, as in the ... of a container

explanation.surface: A book whose contents bring pleasure to its reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the amount a thing holds and, as in 'to one's heart's...', a state of satisfaction.

clue.text: Nothing dropped by political party — hence taxes

indicators.note: dropped by says the zero is lost from the party's name

parts.note: the Tories are the British Conservative Party
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A party abandoning its no-tax pledge, so it raises taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxes' looks like a noun but is the verb: strains or tests.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to strain or test them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Vessel not the same as a cutter

definitions.text: not the same as a cutter
definitions.meaning: a tool for trimming hair or nails, different from a knife or cutting tool

explanation.surface: A sailing ship that is distinct from the class of boat called a cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits two ship types; the second sense is a trimming tool, a word distinct from cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fast nineteenth-century sailing ship and a trimming tool.

clue.text: Many fish stick together

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A shoal of fish keeping close together.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere or hold fast to one another is a synonym of this verb.

clue.text: Monster controlling the middle

indicators.note: the middle points to the inner letters of the word controlling

explanation.surface: A creature dominating the centre ground, as in a game or battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is an ugly giant or monster in Scandinavian folklore.

clue.text: Pained expression when front of pocket is ripped off

indicators.note: front of selects the opening letter of the pocket word for removal
is ripped off says that front letter is torn away

parts.note: a pouch is a pocket

explanation.surface: Someone yelping as their trouser pocket is torn.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation people utter when hurt, so it is an expression of pain.

clue.text: A drop of ink?

parts.note: a spilt drop of ink leaves a stain or mark on the paper

explanation.definitionFit: A stain or spot of ink on paper is what this word names.

clue.text: Change as one ages

indicators.note: Change tells us to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: People alter as they grow older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ages' looks like a verb, growing old, but is the plural noun: very long periods.
explanation.definitionFit: Long eras or vast stretches of time are synonyms for ages.

clue.text: Calm donkey with ague that's run amok

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: run amok means gone wild, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Soothing a donkey suffering a feverish shivering fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or ease pain or anger is a synonym of calm as a verb.

clue.text: Hide in south-east Mediterranean isle

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Going into hiding on a Greek island in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal or stash something away is a synonym for hide.

clue.text: Still out of tune?

definitions.meaning: read as without a tune, an air being a melody

explanation.surface: Asking whether a musician who has stopped is off-key.
explanation.definitionFit: Windless weather is still; and air also means a melody, so the word read differently means tuneless.

clue.text: Abnormal postage brings out the secret police

indicators.note: Abnormal indicates the letters appear in an irregular order

explanation.surface: Odd stamps on a letter attract the attention of security agents.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi secret state police force was known by this name.

clue.text: Where things are washed up or settle on the seabed

definitions.meaning: a kitchen basin where dishes are washed
to go down below the water's surface and come to rest

explanation.surface: Debris washed ashore or settling on the ocean floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed up' suggests a beach but means dishes washed in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen basin for washing up, and the verb for going to the bottom of the sea.

clue.text: At one time part of population census

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that was formerly recorded in a count of residents.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly or in the past, the adverb is a synonym for at one time.

clue.text: Crew employee or member held in affection

definitions.meaning: a deckhand or crew member on a ship
a member of the body that lovers hold

explanation.surface: A sailor who is well liked by the rest of the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker or crew member is a hand, and the body part is a limb that lovers clasp.

clue.text: I study Eastern art

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A student announcing their subject of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' meaning to study is an old word crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious images painted on wood, an art of Eastern Orthodox churches, are known by this word.

clue.text: Carrying on, Mother gets canteen in uproar

indicators.note: uproar means chaos, so the canteen and in are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A mother causing a scene in the works canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in uproar' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is part of the anagram fodder and 'uproar' alone is the signal; 'gets' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something going, or upkeep, is the noun's sense of carrying on.

clue.text: This month in a short way in a short way

definitions.text: This month in a short way

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Repeated phrase like a stuck record: this month, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the same words twice: first as part of the definition (the abbreviation, in short form, for this month), then as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation of instant, old business-letter usage for the current month, is a short form of this month.

clue.text: Description of an eternity ring?

parts.note: an eternity ring is a band of gems all the way round, so it has no finish

explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a circle without a stopping point, and eternity has no finish, so endless describes both.
